summary: Eleven labels print hibiscus flower extract 800 mg, and two cranberry products print hibiscus extract, one at 100 mg and one with no amount; the label rows show no marker content, and the stored record is a narrative review (23333908). Pooled analyses favor hibiscus on blood pressure (39870328, 34927694, 34694241), but their abstracts do not separate extract from tea and give no doses, and one reports no significant effect with metabolic syndrome. For extract capsules specifically, Cochrane found one trial and called the evidence insufficient at very low certainty (34837382), a 108-person RCT at 1000 mg/day was null against placebo on all assessed metabolic parameters and blood pressure (40334927), and a pooled weight analysis was null (38878905). Abstracts only.
